messages:
sasha: Quick postmortem follow-up from yesterday's auth-provider outage — we got through the immediate blast but we still need concrete owners + deadlines for the follow-up items. writing these here so we don't lose them. :spiral_notepad:

mike: thanks. can we split into short-term (hotfixes) and medium-term (runbook + infra changes)?

sasha: yep. short-term: automated fallback to secondary auth, model-registry token cache TTL bump, and clearer delegation for vendor escalations. medium: vendor SLA mapping, circuit-breaker for registry auth calls, and a runbook practice drill.

tara: i'm happy to own the auth fallback wiring (short-term). estimate: PR + deploy by 2026-04-01. i'll add test harness in staging.

omar: i'll take the model-registry cache TTL change and add a monitoring alert for cache thrash. ETA 2026-03-30. patch is minimal (config-only) but need someone to review rollout plan.

mike: i can review and help coordinate canary. also volunteering to draft the vendor escalation playbook (who to call, escalation chain, sample emails). target 2026-04-05.

product-ops: we'll coordinate an exec summary for the affected customers and confirm messaging windows. tentatively ready by 2026-03-31. please attach any technical notes.

eng-sre-bot: Incident 2026-03-22-AP-51 recorded. Follow-up checklist created: fallback-auth, registry-cache, vendor-sla, runbook. Reminders set for owners.

sasha: medium-term items — Omar/Mike: need to design a circuit-breaker at the client layer for model-registry auth calls so bursts from retries don't cascade. Proposal doc due 2026-04-12.

tara: question on fallback: do we prefer OAuth provider B (secondary) or short-lived signed tokens generated by us? both have tradeoffs.

mike: preference = secondary provider for speed, but we should also prototype signed-token fallback as a resilience mode. doc both approaches in the playbook.

sasha: agreed. action list summary (copy this into the postmortem board):
- tara: implement automatic secondary-auth fallback + tests. owner: tara. due: 2026-04-01.
- omar: increase model-registry token cache TTL + monitoring. owner: omar. due: 2026-03-30.
- mike: vendor escalation playbook + runbook skeleton. owner: mike. due: 2026-04-05.
- sasha: coordinate a runbook drill (tabletop) and add rollback/fallback checks. owner: sasha. due: 2026-04-15.
- product-ops: customer comms + post-incident summary. owner: product-ops. due: 2026-03-31.
- eng-sre: add circuit-breaker pattern to client libs (RFC). owner: eng-sre. due: 2026-04-12.

tara: putting these in JIRA now. linking to postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-RES-2345

omar: also noticed a recurring pattern across the last 3 auth blips — spikes at token renewal windows. i suggest we add jitter to refresh logic to spread load. tiny change, high impact.

mike: great catch. please include data in the RFC (histogram of renewal times). we'll prioritize if it reduces crossing vendor rate limits.

product-ops: for customer comms, please flag which accounts had dedicated private deployments vs hosted — different language for SLAs. we'll draft two templates.

sasha: final note: owners, please update the postmortem board and set reminders for status updates. we'll reconvene next Tue 10am PT to verify progress. :eyes: any blockers?

tara: no blockers from infra side. will ping if the staging harness requires GPU infra changes.

omar: will need Mike's review for canary rollout plan. otherwise good.

mike: ack. i'll schedule a 30m sync for Monday if needed.

sasha: thanks everyone. i'll post the consolidated action tracker and assign the Jira tickets by EOD. :white_check_mark:
